title: Research Papers
head: title
line: The research behind our evidence base: the question, the findings and what they mean for investors.

items.title: Do Stocks Outperform Treasury Bills?
items.question: Do stocks generally create wealth through consistent performance, or do a small number of exceptional companies drive most market returns?
findings: A small number of companies create a disproportionate amount of total stock market wealth
Many individual stocks underperform Treasury bills, produce mediocre returns, or destroy investor capital
items.implication: The challenge is not simply to buy stocks. The challenge is to identify businesses capable of exceptional long-term compounding.
items.lesson: A portfolio is not just a collection of companies. It is a collection of future business outcomes.

items.title: Efficient Market Hypothesis
items.question: How efficiently do markets incorporate information into prices?
findings: Markets are highly competitive and difficult to consistently outperform
Information quality matters, behavioural biases exist, and some investors exploit inefficiencies
items.implication: The goal is not predicting everything. The goal is finding areas where understanding is better, time horizon is longer, and behaviour is superior.
items.lesson: Markets are difficult, but not impossible.

items.title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
items.question: How do humans actually make decisions under uncertainty?
findings: Humans feel losses more strongly than gains
Humans evaluate outcomes relative to reference points
items.implication: Many investment mistakes are psychological, not analytical. Investors sell winners too early, hold losers too long, and panic during volatility.
items.lesson: Understanding yourself is part of understanding investing.

items.title: Irrational Exuberance
items.question: Why do markets sometimes become disconnected from fundamentals?
findings: Markets are influenced by narratives, social trends, investor psychology, and media attention
items.implication: Prices are not always determined purely by fundamentals. Human emotion influences markets.
items.lesson: A compelling story can move prices without creating value.

items.title: Security Analysis
items.question: How should investors analyse securities?
findings: Investors should focus on intrinsic value, financial strength, margin of safety, and avoiding speculation
items.implication: Price and value are different concepts.
items.lesson: The investor's job is not finding certainty. It is finding favourable odds.

items.title: On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance
items.question: Can past performance predict future returns?
findings: Momentum has historically shown evidence of persistence as an investment factor
items.implication: Markets are influenced by trends, behaviour, and investor psychology.
items.lesson: Markets are not purely rational systems.

items.title: What Works on Wall Street
items.question: Which investment characteristics historically produced strong returns?
findings: Certain measurable characteristics, including value, quality, and momentum, have historically shown effectiveness
items.lesson: Good investing combines data, judgement, and discipline.

items.title: The Little Book That Still Beats the Market
items.question: Can simple rules identify attractive companies?
findings: Ranking companies on quality and price identifies a systematic set of attractive candidates
items.implication: Great businesses at reasonable prices are attractive.

items.title: Wealth Creation and Concentration
items.question: Where does long-term market wealth come from?
findings: A small percentage of companies create the majority of long-term market wealth
items.lesson: Average companies produce average outcomes. Exceptional businesses create exceptional outcomes.

items.title: Investor Behaviour Studies
items.question: Why do investors often achieve worse returns than the funds they own?
findings: Investor behaviour often reduces returns through poor timing, emotional decisions, and performance chasing
items.implication: Behaviour management is a core investment skill.
items.lesson: A good strategy poorly followed becomes a bad strategy.
